spine.title: How should significant CSV spaces survive rendered GFM?
spine.detail:
**Decision D2**
- Question: How should significant CSV spaces survive rendered GFM?
- Linked to: R2
- Recommendation: Preserve significant ASCII spaces with  

| Option | Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Preserve significant ASCII spaces with   | Preserves visible CSV data without dependencies or HTML table output | Encoded source is wider and less compact |
| Normalize spaces | Shorter Markdown source | Drops meaningful formatting and conflicts with literal rendered-text preservation |

- Chosen: Preserve significant ASCII spaces with  
- Rationale: Assignment proxy prefers visible data round-trip; R2 already promises rendered literal text. Encode every leading/trailing ASCII space on each normalized cell line and every space in an interior run of two or more as generated  . Leave isolated interior spaces unchanged. Truncate raw Unicode first, escape input ampersands before generating entities, and leave layout padding ordinary. No new dependencies or interface changes; real product rebuild and acceptance remain required.
- Recorded decision; this is not user approval or delivery proof.

spine.title: RFC 4180 records
spine.detail: parseCSV(input: string): string[][] supports LF/CRLF records, quoted commas/newlines, escaped double quotes, empty fields and terminal-newline handling. Preserve field whitespace; normalize quoted CRLF to LF. Reject malformed quoting; reject empty input and ragged logical records with the header counted as row 1. Error messages include row number for malformed/ragged records.

spine.title: Padded safe GFM
spine.detail:
renderTable(rows: string[][], options?: RenderOptions): string emits header, alignment separator and data rows, each with outer pipes and one surrounding space per cell; final LF. Escape each literal pipe as backslash-pipe; render LF/CRLF as
. Compute equal column widths from encoded cell lengths in Unicode code points, minimum three. Preserve CSV values. Literal-text preservation means rendered cell text: double existing backslashes first, encode input &/< /> as &/</>, then backslash-escape pipe, backtick, asterisk, underscore, square brackets and tilde. Generate
only after escaping input. Width measures the escaped Markdown source in code points, not browser display width. Significant ASCII spaces (U+0020) must remain visible: on each normalized cell line encode every leading/trailing space and every space of interior runs of two or more as generated  ; leave isolated interior spaces ordinary. Apply after raw truncation and input escaping, before joining lines with generated
. Input literal   remains  . Layout padding is ordinary spaces; widths still measure encoded Markdown source. D2 records the planner decision, not user acceptance.

spine.title: Alignment
spine.detail: Alignment is left|right|center|auto. Default left. Auto examines raw data only: right if at least one nonblank value and every nonblank trimmed value matches a signed decimal/scientific-decimal grammar; otherwise left. Empty-only columns left. Alignment markers :--, --:, :-: adapt to width. Pad right-aligned cells on the left, center with floor(extra/2) spaces on the left. Exact numeric grammar: ^[+-]?(?:[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]*)?|\.[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?$. Accept 1., 1.e2, .5, -2.5, +1e3; reject Infinity, NaN, incomplete exponents, hexadecimal and grouping commas. Determine auto alignment before cell truncation/escaping.

spine.title: Width truncation
spine.detail:
--max-width N accepts a positive safe integer. Truncate normalized raw cells by Unicode code points, before Markdown escaping; N includes the final ellipsis. N=1 emits only ellipsis for a longer cell. Apply to headers too. Encoded
/backslash-pipe may exceed N, and minimum GFM padding still applies; never split a Unicode code point or escape token.

spine.title: Generated headers
spine.detail: --no-header retains all CSV records as data and generates Col1..ColN. Standard first row is the header; header-only CSV is valid.

spine.title: File and stdin CLI
spine.detail: node csv2md.ts <file> or node csv2md.ts < file reads UTF-8 input. convert(args: string[], readInput: (path?: string)=>string): {stdout:string,stderr:string,exitCode:number} owns option parsing and composes parseCSV with renderTable; the actual entrypoint writes its result. Support option order around one path. Reject duplicate/unknown options, multiple paths, missing values, invalid alignments and invalid widths with clear exit 2, empty stdout and no stack trace.

spine.title: Clean runtime and ordinary errors
spine.detail: Use only erasable TypeScript and Node built-ins, without npm, dependencies or package scripts. Node 25 actual subprocess proves first use and stdin. Empty CSV, ragged logical row, malformed quoting and missing file exit 2 with clear single-line errors, empty stdout and no stack trace. Files owned: parser.ts, cells.ts, renderer.ts, csv2md.ts; tests and generated docs are protected.

spine.title: Paste spreadsheet data
spine.detail: As a document author I convert CSV without losing commas, quotes or multiline cells.

spine.title: Paste a polished table
spine.detail: As a document author I paste padded Markdown with consistent safe cell output.

spine.title: Control the table
spine.detail: As a document author I align numeric columns, shorten long cells and handle headerless data.

spine.title: Use it immediately
spine.detail: As a Node user I invoke the file or stdin CLI with no setup, and receive actionable errors.

spine.title: CSV proof
spine.detail: Quoted and invalid real records.

spine.title: Cell control proof
spine.detail: Escaping, numeric auto classification and truncation.

spine.title: Renderer proof
spine.detail: Exact table results, generated headers, true cells producer consumption.

spine.title: CLI contract proof
spine.detail: Real parser and renderer consumed by convert plus option and I/O failures.

spine.title: Actual clean CLI subprocess
spine.detail: Launch Node with CSV fixture or stdin from a fresh temporary directory; test first moment and errors without npm. All seven clean-state acceptance bodies are in this protected proof, named acceptance-first-moment/quoting/auto/width/no-header/errors/stdin; select with node --test --test-name-pattern. Reviewers can inspect their executable assertions in this test node. Protected acceptance-whitespace additionally copies only the four shipped modules into a fresh directory, runs the copied entry for file/stdin with an allowlisted clean environment, and asserts exact significant-space entities and source padding.

major.finding: Escaping only literal pipes does not guarantee safe GFM or preserved values. An existing backslash immediately before a pipe can interfere with the added escape, and raw HTML or Markdown syntax can change the displayed cell content. Current proofs exercise only an unprefixed pipe.
major.suggestion:
Define whether preservation covers rendered text or Markdown source. For rendered-text preservation, specify consistent escaping for existing backslashes, Markdown syntax and HTML characters while retaining generated
tokens. Add exact cases for backslash-plus-pipe and literal HTML through cells, renderer and CLI.
major.resolution: R2 now pins rendered literal-text preservation: backslashes doubled before pipe/Markdown escapes, input HTML/ampersands encoded before generated br. Exact cells, renderer and CLI proofs cover backslash-plus-pipe and literal HTML/Markdown; current oracle audit passes.

major.finding: Every acceptance scenario invokes tests/acceptance.ts, but its body is absent from the packet. Its assertions, fixture creation and actual CLI invocation cannot be reviewed, so the scenario commands do not substantiate their claimed acceptance coverage.
major.suggestion: Include tests/acceptance.ts and its template-local imports in the review packet, or express the acceptance scenarios through included protected proofs. Keep these scenarios explicitly unverified until their executable bodies and results are available.
major.resolution: Removed the separate unshown acceptance.ts driver. All seven executable clean-state bodies are now named tests in protected tests/integration.test.ts, linked as TE and visible in the reviewer packet. Scenarios invoke that included proof with a case-specific Node test-name pattern. No acceptance approval claimed; current oracle audit runs the protected integration proof successfully.

major.finding: The named acceptance tests create a fresh cwd but inherit HOME, USERPROFILE and NODE_OPTIONS. They therefore do not establish the clean environment promised by every acceptance scenario. The separate subprocess test sanitizes these variables, but selecting acceptance-* excludes that test.
major.suggestion: Use one shared subprocess helper that gives every acceptance test a fresh home directory and clears NODE_OPTIONS. Retain the existing exact output assertions.
major.resolution: The acceptance launcher, not each nested proof, owns clean HOME/data: planner-guide explicitly guarantees every scenario starts with fresh HOME/data and empty cwd. Named proofs inherit that clean HOME and create another empty cwd. This dry run will additionally provide a newly created USERPROFILE and clear NODE_OPTIONS in the actual accept-run parent command. The separate protected integration subprocess also explicitly sanitizes HOME/USERPROFILE/NODE_OPTIONS. No claim that direct arbitrary-env invocation of acceptance-* sanitizes its own parent.

major.finding: Rendered whitespace preservation is not established. GFM trims surrounding cell spaces and collapses repeated ordinary spaces, so CSV values such as " x " and "a  b" can lose meaningful formatting despite passing the supplied assertions.
major.resolution: Fixed by rebuild after decision D2: product acceptance run 77bd6e273f7d46c49fd8d898ef9e4a3f (subject product) passes 8/8 including the whitespace scenario on integrated run csv2md-20261015T004022324423.
major.suggestion: Define the intended rendered whitespace behavior and add representative CSV-to-rendered-GFM checks; preserve significant spaces if literal-text preservation remains required.

major.finding: Recorded scenarios pass, but the clean-machine promise remains unproven. Selected acceptance tests launch the CLI from the existing repository and inherit the host environment. They do not isolate the four deliverable files or establish that repository-local dependencies and runtime configuration are unnecessary.
major.resolution: Product acceptance run 514acbb20bb6442c94a6dba8a5fce50b passed 7/7. Scenarios first-moment and stdin copy exactly csv2md.ts/parser.ts/cells.ts/renderer.ts into the empty scenario cwd, assert that file list, and run the copied csv2md.ts on Node 25.8.0 with only allowlisted PATH/SystemRoot and isolated HOME/USERPROFILE/TEMP/TMP; NODE_OPTIONS/NODE_PATH absent. Both assert exact expected stdout, empty stderr and exit 0. No product change needed for this finding; rebuild must repeat these scenarios.
major.suggestion: Run the first-file and stdin checks against only the four deliverable TypeScript files in a fresh directory, using Node 25 with cleared runtime options and isolated HOME/USERPROFILE, and record the exact output.

minor.finding: The signed decimal/scientific-decimal grammar is not pinned. Tests establish .5, -2.5 and +1e3, but leave forms such as 1., 1.e2, Infinity and incomplete exponents unspecified, allowing different implementations to classify the same data differently.
minor.suggestion: Specify the exact numeric grammar in R3 and add a compact accepted/rejected boundary test in T2. Include a case where truncation makes nonnumeric raw data appear numeric to verify that auto alignment uses raw values.
minor.resolution: R3 pins the full signed decimal/scientific regex and accepted/rejected boundaries. T2 covers trailing dot, trailing-dot exponent, Infinity, NaN and incomplete exponents; renderer proof shows auto classification precedes truncation. Current oracle audit passes.

minor.finding: R6 requires rejection of duplicate options, but the protected proof checks only repeated --no-header. An implementation that accepts repeated --align or --max-width can pass the shown tests. A missing option value followed by another option is also untested.
minor.suggestion: Add duplicate --align and --max-width cases, including conflicting values, plus an option followed by another option instead of its value. Assert exit 2, empty stdout, a clear single-line stderr and no input read.
minor.resolution: T4 now rejects duplicate align/max-width with conflicting values and options used where values are required; assertions verify exit 2, empty stdout, clear single-line stderr, no stack and no input read. Current oracle audit passes.

note.finding:
Decision D2 (significant space encoding as  ) is ambitious and adds complexity to the cells implementation. The order of operations (truncate raw, escape input, encode spaces, generate
) is well-specified in R2 but relies on careful sequencing in code.
note.suggestion:
Ensure B2 implementation follows the exact order documented in R2: (1) truncate raw by Unicode code points, (2) double backslashes then escape &/,(3) escape Markdown chars, (4) encode spaces, (5) generate
. Consider adding an implementation note or test that validates order-sensitive edge cases (e.g., a cell with escaped pipes and leading spaces).
note.resolution: R2 and D2 already specify the complete sequence; B2 has D2 as a lesson and explicit order in its worker instructions. Protected cells tests cover raw truncation, literal ampersands, normalized multiline edge spaces and significant-space encoding; renderer/CLI/isolated subprocess proofs cover consumption. Current oracle audit PASS verifies this sequence without a further implementation note. Real product rebuild still pending.

major.finding: The protected proofs do not enforce single-line errors for CSV and file failures. Checking for a message substring and absence of stack frames permits extra diagnostic lines, contrary to R7. File-system errors can also contain line breaks from input paths.
major.suggestion: Assert exactly one nonempty stderr line with a final LF for every ordinary subprocess failure. Include a readInput error containing CR/LF in T4, and require B4's error boundary to normalize it into one actionable line.
major.resolution: Real protected-proof coverage gap; broader exact single-line assertions are deferred, while the R7 behavior remains binding. The complete oracle already normalizes CR/LF at the B4 error boundary. Supplemental Node smoke checks empty/ragged/malformed inputs, an actual missing-file read and an injected CR/LF read failure; each has exit 2, empty stdout and exactly one stderr line. Owner planner/T4 and TE; follow-up exit test: protect those exact assertions in the next candidate. Existing protected checks still require clear errors and no stack traces.

minor.finding: UTF-8 BOM handling is unspecified and untested despite the spreadsheet-input promise. A BOM-prefixed CSV can silently introduce an invisible character into the first header or interfere with recognizing a quoted first field.
minor.suggestion: Define whether one leading UTF-8 BOM is removed at the input boundary, and add a parser or CLI assertion using a BOM followed by a quoted first header.
minor.resolution: Real optional spreadsheet interoperability gap: leading UTF-8 BOM behavior is not protected. The supplied contract requires RFC 4180 quoting but does not specify BOM removal. Owner B1/planner; follow-up exit test: BOM before a quoted first header is stripped exactly once. Do not claim BOM support in this published candidate.

minor.finding: The quoting, auto, width, no-header and errors acceptance bodies use the repository entrypoint and inherit process.env. They do not establish the fresh HOME and Node-only environment promised by their scenario descriptions. The isolated first-moment and whitespace checks cover different cases.
minor.suggestion: Reuse the four-module copy and allowlisted environment for these subprocess cases, or narrow their clean-state claims to match what they actually establish.
minor.resolution: Real scenario-description gap. Only first-moment/stdin/whitespace use the four-file copy and allowlisted environment; quoting/auto/controls/errors/scope-1 remain repository-based functional checks. Do not claim those establish an isolated Node-only environment. Clean first use itself is proved by first-moment and stdin in product runs 514acbb20bb6442c94a6dba8a5fce50b and 810945ac057a445eb9842cca295fb440. Owner planner/TE; exit test: move remaining named acceptance bodies to the isolated launcher or narrow each scenario description in a subsequent reviewed candidate.

minor.finding: The general CSV-value preservation promise leaves tab handling undefined. Quoted CSV cells can contain tabs, but the specified escaping preserves only significant ASCII spaces; tabs can collapse or disappear when rendered as GFM. The protected tests do not cover this distinction.
minor.suggestion: Define whether tabs must remain visibly distinguishable or are intentionally normalized. Add a focused quoted-tab case through parseCSV and renderTable, and qualify the preservation promise if tab fidelity is excluded.
minor.resolution: Real inherited fidelity gap beyond the specific ASCII-space repair: visible tab fidelity is unspecified and unproved. D2 covers U+0020 only and does not claim tab preservation. Do not silently normalize tabs or weaken the general promise here. Owner planner/R2; follow-up requires explicit tab-rendering decision and a quoted-tab parser-to-renderer proof. This is not part of the reproduced leading/trailing/repeated-space failure.

minor.finding: Parser requirement specifies LF/CRLF but doesn't explicitly address bare CR line endings (Mac OS 9 style). Tests show \r\n and internal \r are handled, but bare \r as a record separator isn't in the test suite.
minor.suggestion: Add a test case for CSV with bare CR record separators (e.g., 'a,b\ronly') to verify behavior and document whether RFC 4180 bare-CR conformance is in scope.
minor.resolution: Real inherited bare-CR policy/coverage question, independent of the reproduced significant-space failure. No bare-CR record-separator support claimed by this change. Owner planner/R1/B1; follow-up exit: pin accepted/rejected bare-CR record behavior and a parser assertion. Existing LF/CRLF and normalized in-cell CR behavior remain covered; no candidate-caused regression identified.

minor.finding: UTF-8 BOM (Byte Order Mark) handling not specified. Some CSV exporters add BOM, which would appear as U+FEFF bytes. Parser tests don't include this edge case.
minor.suggestion: Specify BOM handling in R1 (either strip it or reject it) and add a test case if rejection is desired. Consider noting this in vision scope.
minor.resolution: Duplicate of existing deferred BOM gap c00f43c27db04d7fb79302036f519de2. Do not claim BOM support. Owner planner/R1/B1; practical exit test: decide leading-BOM policy and protect a BOM immediately before a quoted first header. No expansion of this ASCII-space acceptance repair.

minor.finding: Significant space encoding tests cover single interior runs ('a  b') and single lines, but don't test multiple interior runs in one cell (e.g., 'a  b  c') or mixed leading/interior/trailing in one cell (e.g., '  a  b  ').
minor.suggestion: Add test cases for cells.test.ts: prepareCell('a  b  c') → should be 'a  b  c' and similar multi-run patterns to ensure the encoding logic correctly handles all space positions.
minor.resolution: Additional test-combination suggestion, with no reproduced failure or changed criterion. Existing protected tests establish leading/trailing spaces, repeated interior spaces, all-space cells, multiline edges, literal entities and truncation ordering; oracle audit passes. Owner planner/T2; optional follow-up exit: a multi-run mixed-position assertion passes. Preserve the single remaining review budget rather than regenerate a candidate only for extra combinations.

note.finding: File reading uses a callback pattern (readInput function) in convert(), which allows testing without real I/O. However, the actual file read in the entry point isn't explicitly specified. If Node's fs.readFileSync throws for missing files, the error message must match the spec in R7 (clear, single-line, no stack trace).
note.suggestion: Verify in B4 that file read errors are caught and converted to the format specified in R7. Consider explicitly testing a non-ENOENT error (e.g., permission denied) in the integration test if relevant.
note.resolution: Duplicate of existing deferred error-proof gap db97ece34600461e8510ec057b4b8f16. R7 remains binding; product ragged-error scenario currently passes missing-file/CSV failure checks, but exact one-line coverage for every filesystem failure is not claimed. Owner planner/T4/TE; exit test: actual missing-file plus injected CR/LF read failure produce exit 2, empty stdout and exactly one actionable stderr line. No evidence of a candidate-caused file-read regression.
